Staff were notified prior to his arrival that the youth had gone to a mental health crisis center today and were encouraged to be aware of his behavior and his explanation for the visit. JG arrived at The Source and was withholding about the events of his day. During arrival, the youth verbally resisted the pocket check and bag check but ultimately complied with staff instruction. Staff collected new meds from the youth and added them to the MAR. Staff then informed JG that he needed to have a conversation with staff to set expectations for the night and to check-in about his visit to the crisis center. _x000A__x000A_During this conversation, the youth was slow to respond to staff questions and resistant to sharing the reason for his visit to the crisis center. JG was adamant that he was not experiencing suicidality and could contract for safety at the shelter. JG also offered a way that staff could support him in completing his chore. At some point, the youth became less defensive and shared some personal events that have been distressing JG. _x000A__x000A_Following this conversation, staff checked in with on-call and they suggested that youth fill out Safety Plan sheet in addition to writing on the back of the sheet the reason for the visit to the crisis center. Youth was polite from this point forward and started filling out the Safety Plan right away. Youth expressed regret in his initial behavior when arriving. Youth completed safety plan within an appropriate amount of time. _x000A__x000A_Later, staff had a deep conversation with JG about coping mechanisms, staff put forward that we are all human beings, and being angry or sad is something natural that may come up again in the future, that being said JG and staff agreed that we should have a plan if there is escalation again. JG opened up about his past and the problems with him showing his emotion by crying, staff talked with him and assured him crying is a healthy mechanism. JG seemed very receptive to the conversation._x000A__x000A_Important to note- JG told staff about a conversation he had with EP off property where he told EP he was a virgin and EP laughed at him. Staff reminded him not to talk about sexual topics with those not wishing to discuss and further reminded him not to reference those topics on property. Staff wrapped up the conversation with a discussion about the importance of boundaries.

In the morning, was very polite with staff and reported he was feeling positive and was happy to be here. He said he wanted to stay in Boulder, go to school, find a job, and find housing. Staff talked with him about finishing his GED and informed him that if he wants to go to college afterwards there are grants and financial aid options available. Informed staff that he talked with his family in Nebraska, something which was contributing to his positive mood. He also said his abusive mother was coming to the U.S., but was going to stay in Nebraska. He is worried about this but he reported feeling safe here. Staff validated his feelings and told him that if he feels unsafe we can help him safety plan. Talked with him about his medications and when he should take the new ones that he brought._x000A__x000A_Came to staff office door and said "I'm going to say this while he's listening, I have a problem with Justin". JR was sitting in earshot, but did not respond. Staff shut it down right away. Told him if he wanted a mediation, we could do that, but JR would also have to agree. Also gave him a warning to not talk about it in the space as this could earn him strikes. After having a conversation w/ ZH and JR, staff talked to JG. JG said he is depressed that he lost ZH as a friend and he thinks JR is a bad influence because "she cusses more". Told him JR was not interested in a mediation, but discussed different ways in which he can take space for himself while on property such as listening to music and working on his GED. He asked what he should do if JR starts to become escalated off property. Told him to try to put his headphones on, listen to music, and walk away. Reminded him that if he feels unsafe he can call the police. He said he doesn't like to get the police involved, to which staff validated his feelings, but said he would walk away and come back here. Staff told him this was a good plan. He also said he's concerned that if he hangs out with ZH too much he could become a suspect or she would accuse him of something. Told him this probably wouldn't happen, but encouraged him to keep his distance anyway due to all the drama. Asked him if he's made any other friends here. He mentioned ND and NW. Encouraged him to hang out with them, take his own space, and try to stay away from ZH and JR._x000A__x000A_Gave him the gift card for King Soopers to buy a pair of glasses. Printed out directions for him. Told him to bring back the receipt

Used the King Soopers gift card to buy reading glasses - provided receipt for proof (placed in "to be filed" folder). Came to staff saying he was "threatened". Showed staff a text reportedly from JR's phone, but he claimed ZH sent it. It said he was "a piece of shit" for talking to staff in the morning about the drama between him and JR. It also said "you are paying for the phone", and said that he broke someone's phone._x000A__x000A_Reminded him he needs to check in w/ Nic tomorrow as it's a condition of his stay. Became pretty upset by this. He said that he didn't need to see that many people and it was too much for him on top of all the other appointments he has. He mentioned his friend Hope is a therapist and regularly sees her. Validated his feelings, but reminded him it's a condition of his stay. At first he thought he was going to talk to Nic about LGBTQ+ topics and said he didn't need that because he now understands it. Told him that wasn't the case and it was just to check in and develop coping mechanisms to help him feel happier. He reluctantly agreed but still said it was too much. Told him he could talk to PM about it._x000A__x000A_Told staff his leg was hurting him and that he had a bump that was hitting the bone. Staff administered Tylenol. He expressed desire to get it checked out tonight, so staff told him we could give him bus passes to get to the hospital. Printed out directions and told him which bus stop to use and which busses to take. He did not want to take the bus by himself and claimed he was in so much pain we needed to call an ambulance. Told him that we could only call an ambulance for an emergency. He was standing up perfectly fine and staff saw him walking around before and after the conversation. He gave the bus passes back and stood at the staff office door for a few minutes before saying "you think I'm lying". Staff told him that's not the case, but we can't justify calling an ambulance. He said he was calling 911. Staff couldn't stop him, but got him to wait outside while he called._x000A__x000A_A firetruck and an ambulance arrived around 10 minutes later, On-call notified, Youth reminded to bring in discharge paperwork upon return(staff also asked paramedics to remind JG). Paramedics seemed to be more concerned with his mental state vs his leg, asking what medications he is currently taking and if he has any personality disorders._x000A__x000A_JG returned at 10:34 and provided discharge paperwork, paperwork confirms JG only had a bruise. JG also reports that once they discharged him they sent him to a mental hospital, where he then left and was driven here by a stranger._x000A__x000A_Later in the night, JG came into the staff office and asked why JR can walk around "the way he is" but he cant be more open by his religion. Also in reference to the PM, JG stated, "ill talk with your boss Monday, I don't care if she is a killer"

Divalproex: 42_x000A_Olanzapine: 13_x000A_Hydroxyzine: 49_x000A_Omeprazole: 15_x000A_Penicillin: 12_x000A_Loperamide: 30_x000A_Azithromycin: out - but was only prescribed for one dose_x000A__x000A_Told staff he doesn't trust all the staff. Had a conversation with him about different communication styles and assured him that all staff here care and want to make sure he is safe, but all staff members communicate that differently. He also said ND told him staff were bad people and told him "to get out of here". Talked with him about how sometimes people try to make jokes but it doesn't come out as a joke. Before he had finished taking the full bags out of the trash cans, he became escalated with staff saying that he no longer trusted them because he was feeling triggered. At the start of house meeting, JG became escalated and refused to participate. He explained to staff that his PTSD was being triggered and he exhibited warning signs he had noted in his TISP. As he continued to escalate, staff recommended that he leave house meeting and go back upstairs. He received 1 strike for not completing house meeting. _x000A__x000A_Upon leaving house meeting, staff overheard JG calling 911 and reporting "harassment" by a couple of his peers at shelter (ZH, JR). He referenced a threatening text message to emergency response. Staff inquired how emergency response responded and JG stated that a police officer would be speaking to him about his concerns. Staff was unsure whether this meant an officer would be calling him back or coming to meet him on property. JG explained the conflict he is having with these individuals. Again, he referenced a text message received from JR's phone number but penned by ZH. Staff understood this text message to be something that has been addressed by staff in the week(s) previous. JG also spoke about the incident that occurred during house meeting and spoke about being triggered when he observed JR and ZH talking to one another during the meeting. _x000A__x000A_JG was prompted to complete his chore for the night. As he began the chore, JG started to focus on the compost bin in the dining room. He then called staff over and became distressed about the presence of arugula in the bin. JG seemed to be distressed because he didn't know what arugula was and assumed it was marijuana. In response to this distress, JG attempted to do a more thorough clean of the dining room floor by mopping with more water than necessary. Staff then asked that he clean up the excess water. JG complied after staff googled an image of arugula and explained it was not marijuana. JG then proceeded to mop up the excess water using a towel._x000A__x000A_An officer arrived at shelter later in the night and spoke to JG individually in response to his 911 call. The officer then came in to debrief with staff. The officer noted that JG is unhappy with his medication dosage. He also noted that he passed on JG's information to the local Crisis Intervention Response Team as they could have some resources to support him. _x000A__x000A_JG started to head upstairs to bed and staff noticed he had not taken his nightly psychotropic medication. Staff redirected him to the office an in effort to speak about his nightly meds. As staff encouraged JG to take his scheduled medications, JG became increasingly agitated threatening to call the Crisis Center if we "forced" him to take his medications, along with several minutes of highly tangential, nonsensical speech. Staff reminded him that no one can force him to take these medications but that if he refused these medications he would earn a strike. Ultimately, JG took one of his PRNs but none of his scheduled medications and thus earned a strike. He went to bed after this incident. Plans to go to the crisis center in Denver tomorrow to have his medication dosage reduced- as he believes it to be causing unwanted changes in his behavior.

JG spoke of this other resident taking his picture around the shelter. JG spoke to the Colorado Crisis Line over the phone; JG repeatedly requested a CIRT worker to come to the shelter to speak with in-person, but the crisis worker over the phone said they would not send someone out unless JG would talk over the phone first. The crisis line referred JG to both Boulder Community Health and The Collective for Psychological Wellness, to which JG stated he would try to visit one of them today for evaluation of his medications. JG then requested to speak to on-call on the phone; staff called on-call twice and left a voicemail. Had a brief discussion with Ct about getting her connected to Rocky Mountain Equality. Ct was not in a state to have coherent conversations so staff decided not to engaged in any goal setting or further case management until Ct was in a more coherent state of mind.

Ct arrived to drop in center, appeared to be more coherent as evidenced by less responsive to internal stimuli and able to engage in more conversation with staff. Ct was hoping to do a housing assessment with her case manager, but due to the business of the day, the CM was unable to complete a housing assessment and Ct will return to drop in center on a different day to do that. Ct was able to work with YSS Maggie on getting a secured email address and reaching out to Rocky Mountain Equality to get assistance with name change on identification documents. Ct enjoyed a meal with us and took a shower before leaving drop in to head to Samaritan house in Denver for the evening
Met with client to prepare treatment plan

New client requested case management support for assistance with housing. Client had also requested similar support the previous week. During prior contact, client appeared significantly distracted and minimally engaged, with presentation suggestive of internal preoccupation. Client was observed responding to internal stimuli, including possible auditory hallucinations. CM was able to complete a housing assessment with the client today and discuss housing-related goals. Client engaged in the assessment process and participated in identifying current needs and priorities. Youth reported plans to seek shelter placement at Samaritan House in Denver.
